findings.issue_text: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:239 copies existing query results under a fresh revision, potentially republishing stale organization results if an IDP update invalidates the cache between reading query and obtaining loaded. Preserve and validate the original query revision, or reload results before merging.

OrganizationCacheTest.java:381 registers cleanup with the literal alias "alias" instead of each created provider's actual "idp-alias-N" alias, including provider 20. This leaves test providers behind and can cause a 404 or delete an unrelated provider.

goldens.comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

adjudication_records.issue_text: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:239 copies existing query results under a fresh revision, potentially republishing stale organization results if an IDP update invalidates the cache between reading query and obtaining loaded. Preserve and validate the original query revision, or reload results before merging.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a potential race condition in the cache update logic at lines 230-239. When query is not null but cached is null (the search key isn't cached yet), the code invalidates the cache, gets a new revision, fetches fresh results, then creates a new IdentityProviderListQuery passing the old 'query' object to merge its existing results. If another thread invalidated/updated the cache between when we read the original query and when we call cache.addRevisioned(), we could be republishing stale data from the old query under a fresh revision. The code doesn't validate that the original query's revision is still valid before merging its contents into the new query.
